subject: POC access & success criteria — BrightHealth
content:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.ng@brighthealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-25T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: POC access & success criteria — BrightHealth

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the intro call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get the POC rolling:

Goals / success criteria (proposed)
- Validate latency and cost for the claims anonymization pipeline (target: median latency < 150ms per request, < $0.0008/token equivalent)
- Verify model output fidelity on our 5 canonical prompt sets (precision on entity masking >= 98%)
- Confirm integration with BrightHealth SSO and ability to manage keys via customer KMS

Scope & timeline
- 2 week evaluation window starting when BrightHealth team has API access (we can be flexible)
- Week 1: baseline runs + integration (SSO invite + API key for service account)
- Week 2: stress tests, cost profiling, and QA checks against the prompt suite

Ownership
- Redwood: Marissa (project exec) + Aditya (solutions lead) + Dylan (customer success)
- BrightHealth: Sara (technical lead) + James (security/compliance)

Access needed from BrightHealth
1) IP allowlist for our test service IPs (template attached)
2) SSO invite: IdP details (SAML metadata or Okta org) or allow a test service account
3) Provide a short list of sample data endpoints or a small dataset we can run the prompt suite against (synthesized if required)

Attachments: redwood-poc-reqs.pdf (POC checklist), ip-allowlist-template.csv

Proposed next steps
- Sara: confirm you can share SSO metadata and IP allowlist by EOD Monday 6/29
- Aditya: once we have SSO/IP, will provision test service account and generate API key (scoped to test env)
- Dylan: schedule walkthrough for analytics dashboard and cost/latency dashboards

If this looks good I'll send a short mutual action plan and a shared Drive folder for the artifacts.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

---

From: Sara Nguyen <sara.ng@brighthealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: James Park <james.park@brighthealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-25T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC access & success criteria — BrightHealth

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. We agree with the proposed success criteria; a couple quick notes:
- For latency, we care most about 95th percentile for small payloads (<= 2 KB) — can you include p95 in the dashboard?
- On data: we will provide a small synthesized dataset this week; not full production data.

On the security side: James will own SSO/KMS discussions. James — can you confirm if BrightHealth can accept an Okta app invite and if you need us to send a vendor onboarding package?

Also adding one constraint: our compliance team generally requires API keys to be scoped and rotated after the POC. Will that be supported?

Thanks,
Sara Nguyen
Director, AI Engineering — BrightHealth

---

From: James Park <james.park@brighthealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sara Nguyen <sara.ng@brighthealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-26T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC access & success criteria — BrightHealth

Marissa / team —

We can accept an Okta app invite. For KMS we prefer customer-managed keys (we will share KMS ARN). API keys must be scoped to test and will be rotated after 14 days. Also will need an IP allowlist for inbound traffic to our test endpoints (we'll open specific ports).

I'll coordinate with our platform team and aim to send SAML metadata + KMS ARN by Monday 6/29.

Thanks,
James Park
Security & Platform — BrightHealth

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.ng@brighthealth.com>, James Park <james.park@brighthealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-26T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC access & success criteria — BrightHealth

Hi Sara / James —

Great — high level on our side for provisioning:
- SSO: we can accept SAML metadata or an Okta app. Once we have metadata, we'll create a Redwood test org and invite your team. SSO groups can map to RBAC (we'll keep the POC role minimal).
- KMS: we support customer KMS for key wrapping. If you send the ARN we will configure the service account to use it.
- API key / service account: we'll provision a scoped service account and generate a short-lived API key (valid 14 days) for the POC. Rotation/expiry is supported.
- IP allowlist: attached is the template we prefer; please drop your public IPs and any CIDR ranges.

Security contact: adding Vivek (Vivek.Kulkarni@redwood.com) from our security team to support any compliance questions or network runbooks.

Deliverables from Redwood (target within 48 hours of receiving SAML + IPs + KMS ARN):
1) Redwood test org + Okta invite
2) Scoped service account + API key (14-day TTL)
3) Shared Drive with sample prompts and test harness

Let us know if you'd like a short call to walk through the provisioning steps.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-06-27T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC access & success criteria — BrightHealth

Hi all —

Quick note on measurement and evaluation:
- We'll run the 5 canonical prompts across 3 representative payload sizes and capture token counts, latency (p50/p95), and output fidelity.
- I'll share a small evaluation script (Python) that pushes test requests and collates results into the dashboard.
- Post-POC checklist: decisions on model variant, quantization profile, and recommended batch/throughput settings.

I'll schedule the first run for the morning after access is provisioned and share preliminary results within 48 hours.

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
